chunks: 3016 - He said: And I heard him saying regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"So whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him, for the one who is Godwary."
So he said: "He avoids hunting until the people of Minā depart in the final departure."

key_terms.اتَّقَىٰ: being Godwary; here, observing the required restraint during the rites
key_terms.الصَّيْدَ: hunting game, which must be avoided here until the final departure
key_terms.النَّفْرِ الْأَخِيرِ: the final departure from Minā after the prescribed days
key_terms.تَأَخَّرَ: delayed departure to the later permitted time
key_terms.تَعَجَّلَ: hastened to leave earlier within the permitted time
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the place where pilgrims remain during these days of hajj

ai.seo_question: What does "for the one who is Godwary" mean in Qur'an 2:203 during the days of Minā?
ai.summary: This report explains the phrase "for the one who is Godwary" in the verse as referring to avoiding hunting during the remaining days in Minā. It clarifies a practical hajj ruling tied to taqwa and the timing of the final departure. The verse is thus interpreted here in connection with conduct during the rites of hajj.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3016 - He said, and I heard him say regarding the verse of Allah (swt), the Exalted:
"Whoever hastens to leave in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him—for the one who is conscious (of Allah (swt))." (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:203):
"It means that one should avoid hunting until the people of Mina depart on the final day of departure (nafr al-akhir)."
